analysis: Reviewed scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py (offline CI workflow unit test). The supplied evidence is the base text of the file plus a truncated patch excerpt. The visible change adds a PROVIDER_SHARDS constant and reworks test_lanes_are_independent_on_dedicated_supported_mac_runners. Per-shard route lanes (test-provider-N, selected via format('test-provider-{0}', matrix.shard)) replace a single shared route lane, and fail-fast: false is asserted. This is test-only code that asserts CI workflow structure. It touches no provider runtime, key custody, attestation, coordinator protocol or prefix-cache code, so it does not change T-041, TB-002, TB-007, TB-009 or TB-011 behavior. The tests still assert no secrets, no backend credentials, no continue-on-error, pinned action SHAs and fail-closed gates. No weakened security assertion is visible in the shown excerpt. Limits: the patch excerpt is truncated, the head file text and the ci.yml and route changes are not supplied, and the tests assert on route and workflow files outside this batch. Integration should confirm that ci.yml and the route job actually produce per-shard routes, and that the gate job (Provider Tests) still requires every shard and the summary job. A mismatch would only affect CI correctness and the sandbox runner routing trust boundary, not the threat model assets directly. I found no concrete security regression in the visible changes.
